patch_description: Replace the returned single-sample greedy with a beam search over transaction orderings. Each beam state holds a partial sequence and its makespan cost; at each step we expand every state with all remaining transactions, evaluate via `get_opt_seq_cost`, and keep the best `beam_width` states. Beam search directly optimizes actual makespan (not proxies like length/write-count), corrects greedy mistakes by keeping several candidates alive, and is far more sample-efficient than random restarts of a 1-sample greedy. We use a depth-adaptive width (wide early, e.g. 6–12, where pruning error compounds most; narrow late, e.g. 3) and run a few restarts with different initial transactions for diversity, keeping the best overall schedule.
